claim: A Cre-dependent APEX2 reporter mouse line was generated using CRISPR/Cas9 knock-in at the Gt(ROSA)26 locus.
source: We created a Cre-dependent APEX reporter mouse line for broad applications in neuroscience and biology. A monomeric APEX2 variant was chosen because of its small size and efficient activity for proximity labeling of proteins (Lam et al., 2015). A double-floxed inverted orientation of the APEX transgene (DIO-APEX2-P2A-EGFP) was introduced into the Gt(ROSA)26 locus under the EF1a promoter using CRISPR/Cas9 strategy (Figure 1a).
evidence: The manuscript describes the creation of the mouse line using specific molecular biology techniques and provides methodological details.

claim: Eight out of 112 founder mutants were identified by genotyping PCR.
source: We identified 8 out 112 founder mutants by genotyping PCR (Figure 1b, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Direct statement of experimental results with reference to supporting figure.

claim: The APEX transgene shows Cre-dependent expression confirmed by genomic DNA PCR.
source: We performed direction-specific PCR to assess Cre-dependent inversion of the APEX transgene using genomic DNA that was directly extracted from the cortex. Inverted transgene was only detected in Cre-expressing brain tissues (Figure 1e), confirming Cre-dependent recombination.
evidence: Experimental validation through PCR analysis showing Cre-dependent recombination.

claim: APEX2 was engineered to be highly efficient for rapid protein biotinylation within seconds to minutes in the presence of hydrogen peroxides.
source: APEX2 was engineered to be highly efficient for rapid protein biotinylation within seconds to minutes in the presence of hydrogen peroxides (Lam et al., 2015), providing superior labeling speed over other proximity labeling methods (Hung et al., 2016; Lobingier et al., 2017).
evidence: Statement supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Corticostriatal projections arise in the embryonic period and continue to innervate the striatum postnatally.
source: In rodents, corticostriatal projections arise in the embryonic period and continue to innervate the striatum postnatally (Nisenbaum et al., 1998; Sheth et al., 1998; Sohur et al., 2014), where growth cones start to disappear around postnatal day P7, based on the reduction of growth-associated protein 43 (GAP43) immunostaining (Dani et al., 1991).
evidence: Statement supported by multiple literature citations.

claim: Growth cones in the striatum start to disappear around postnatal day P7 based on reduction of GAP43 immunostaining.
source: In rodents, corticostriatal projections arise in the embryonic period and continue to innervate the striatum postnatally (Nisenbaum et al., 1998; Sheth et al., 1998; Sohur et al., 2014), where growth cones start to disappear around postnatal day P7, based on the reduction of growth-associated protein 43 (GAP43) immunostaining (Dani et al., 1991).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to prior experimental work.

claim: Biotin phenol incubation time was increased to 2 minutes to optimize protein labeling in thick brain tissue.
source: We increased BP incubation time to 2 min from previously published APEX-mediated biotinylation protocols to optimize protein labeling in thick brain tissue (Dumrongprechachan et al., 2021), since APEX has been largely characterized and applied in cell culture (Hung et al., 2016; Lobingier et al., 2017; Paek et al., 2017) and small organisms (Chen et al., 2015; Reinke et al., 2017).
evidence: Description of methodological modification with citation to prior work.

claim: The level of biotinylation in Vglut2Cre PFC sample was greater than that of VgatCre, consistent with a greater number of glutamatergic neurons relative to GABAergic neurons present in the neocortex.
source: As expected, the level of biotinylation in Vglut2Cre PFC sample was greater than that of VgatCre, consistent with a greater number of glutamatergic neurons relatively to GABAergic neurons present in the neocortex, since under ~20% of cortical neurons are GABAergic (Keller et al., 2018).
evidence: Experimental observation explained by known cellular composition with citation.

claim: Under 20% of cortical neurons are GABAergic.
source: As expected, the level of biotinylation in Vglut2Cre PFC sample was greater than that of VgatCre, consistent with a greater number of glutamatergic neurons relatively to GABAergic neurons present in the neocortex, since under ~20% of cortical neurons are GABAergic (Keller et al., 2018).
evidence: Statement of established fact with citation.

claim: The Rbp4Cre mouse line expresses Cre recombinase under the control of the retinol binding protein 4 (Rbp4) gene promoter.
source: The Rbp4Cre mouse line expresses Cre recombinase under the control of the retinol binding protein 4 (Rbp4) gene promoter.
evidence: Description of genetic tool characteristics.

claim: Rbp4Cre shows Cre-mediated reporter expression enriched in the accessory olfactory bulb, layer 5 pyramidal tract neurons throughout the neocortex, and hippocampal granule cells in the dentate gyrus.
source: A previous characterization of this line shows Cre-mediated reporter expression, enriched in the accessory olfactory bulb, layer 5 pyramidal tract neurons throughout the neocortex, and hippocampal granule cells in the dentate gyrus (Harris et al., 2014).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to prior characterization study.

claim: EGFP reporter expression is observed in the striatum throughout postnatal time period P5-P40 in Rbp4Cre;APEX animals.
source: We showed that EGFP reporter expression is observed in the striatum throughout postnatal time period P5-P40 (Figure 3a).
evidence: Direct observation from experimental data with figure reference.

claim: Western blot analysis after ex vivo biotinylation detects labeled proteins in both cortical and striatal tissues above the negative control, including at the earliest P5 time point.
source: Western blot analysis after ex vivo biotinylation detects labeled proteins in both cortical and striatal tissues above the negative control, including at the earliest P5 time point (Figure 3b, Figure 3—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: Experimental results from Western blot analysis.

claim: No somatic expression was observed in the striatum; therefore, biotinylated proteins in the striatal lysates represent corticostriatal axonal proteins.
source: No somatic expression was observed in the striatum; therefore, biotinylated proteins in the striatal lysates represent corticostriatal axonal proteins.
evidence: Inference based on observed expression pattern.

claim: 5582 proteins were identified and 2276 out of 2709 proteins were quantified without missing values across conditions.
source: We identified 5582 proteins and quantified 2276 out of 2709 proteins without missing values across conditions (Figure 3d Supplementary file 4).
evidence: Direct statement of proteomics results.

claim: Proteins with q-value <0.05 and log2FC >0 were considered axonally enriched.
source: Proteins with q-value <0.05 and log2FC >0 were considered axonally enriched, depicted in the volcano plot (Figure 3f).
evidence: Description of analytical criteria used.

claim: 1129 axon-enriched proteins and 1577 somato-nuclear proteins were classified, with 30% and 17.4% having GO-axon annotations, respectively.
source: Using this criterion, we loosely classified axonal proteins in the dataset into 1129 axon-enriched proteins and 1577 somato-nuclear proteins, with 30% and 17.4% having GO-axon annotations, respectively (Figure 3g).
evidence: Results from classification analysis with GO annotation rates.

claim: The majority of the detected proteome was highly dynamic, with 1981 out of 2274 proteins significantly changing (adjusted p-values < 0.05).
source: As expected, the majority of the detected proteome was highly dynamic, with 1981 out of 2274 proteins significantly changing (adjusted p-values < 0.05).
evidence: Statistical analysis results from maSigPro analysis.

claim: Doublecortin (DCX) rapidly decreases during development.
source: As expected, an immature neuronal marker like microtubule-associated protein DCX rapidly decreases during development, while mature neuronal markers such as medium intermediate filament (NEFM) and other synaptic and vesicle markers (SYP, VGLUT1, and RAB3A) increase over time.
evidence: Observation from data analysis consistent with known developmental patterns.

claim: Mature neuronal markers such as NEFM, SYP, VGLUT1, and RAB3A increase over time during development.
source: As expected, an immature neuronal marker like microtubule-associated protein DCX rapidly decreases during development, while mature neuronal markers such as medium intermediate filament (NEFM) and other synaptic and vesicle markers (SYP, VGLUT1, and RAB3A) increase over time.
evidence: Observation from data analysis consistent with known developmental patterns.

claim: Greater than 65% of the overlapping proteome between any pair of studies change in the same direction in meta-analysis comparison.
source: We found that >65% of the overlapping proteome between any pair of studies change in the same direction (85% for adult, 65% for earlypostnatal, and 69% for preweanling comparison, respectively) (Supplementary file 7).
evidence: Results from meta-analysis comparing multiple studies.

claim: Clusters 2, 3, 5, and 6 were enriched in ASD, BP, EP, and AD risk genes, respectively.
source: We found that clusters 2, 3, 5, and 6 were enriched in ASD, BP, EP, and AD risk genes, respectively (Figure 4d, Supplementary file 9).
evidence: Results from hypergeometric testing for disease risk gene enrichment.

claim: Epilepsy risk genes are significantly enriched in protein cluster 5 (p-value = 0.022).
source: For example, we found that epilepsy risk genes are significantly enriched in protein cluster 5 (p-value = 0.022), which is composed of proteins with increasing expression over time.
evidence: Statistical result from enrichment analysis.

claim: Cluster 5 contains genes enriched in AMPAR trafficking and plasticity (p=1.1e-9).
source: Cluster 5 also contains genes enriched in α-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid receptor (AMPAR) trafficking and plasticity (p=1.1e-9), linking epilepsy risk genes in this cluster to excitatory glutamatergic transmission.
evidence: Statistical result from pathway enrichment analysis.

claim: Reduced corticostriatal excitatory transmission to fast-spiking interneurons was found to trigger absence seizures in Stxbp1 haplodeficient mouse model.
source: In fact, reduced corticostriatal excitatory transmission to fast-spiking interneurons was found to trigger absence seizures in Stxbp1 haplodeficient mouse model and this effect was mitigated by pharmacological activation of AMPAR in striatum (Miyamoto et al., 2019).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to prior experimental study.

claim: The majority of kinases increase in expression over time during development.
source: We found that the majority of kinases increase in expression over time, such as CAMK and AGC families.
evidence: Observation from KEGG pathway analysis of the data.

claim: Some kinases (PAK2, PAK3, PAK5, GSK3B, SSH2, SRC, and FYN) show elevated expression during neonatal and early postnatal time points, but decrease in expression over time.
source: However, some kinases (e.g. PAK2, PAK3, PAK5, GSK3B, SSH2, SRC, and FYN) show elevated expression during neonatal and early postnatal time points, but decrease in expression over time, suggesting a functional relevance for early axon guidance.
evidence: Observation from data analysis with functional interpretation.

claim: DCC expression decreases over time, reflected by negative log2 fold change in the early postnatal and adult samples compared to the neonate.
source: Our data show that DCC expression decreases over time, reflected by negative log2 fold change in the early postnatal and adult samples compared to the neonate.
evidence: Direct observation from the dataset.

claim: SRC and FYN kinases are upregulated during the early postnatal period and downregulated in adulthood.
source: Similarly, SRC and FYN kinases are upregulated during the early postnatal period and downregulated in the adulthood.
evidence: Direct observation from the dataset.

claim: The timing of SRC and FYN upregulation in the early postnatal time coincides with high DCC expression, implicating SRC and FYN as primary regulators of DCC signaling in the neonatal and early postnatal time windows.
source: The timing of SRC and FYN upregulation in the early postnatal time coincides high DCC expression, implicating SRC and FYN as primary regulators of DCC signaling in the neonatal and early postnatal time windows, but not in the adult with matured striatal circuits.
evidence: Inference based on temporal correlation in the data.

claim: 2353 unique phosphopeptides were quantified that were mapped to 708 proteins.
source: After stringently remove peptides with any missing TMT intensity in any sample, we quantified 2353 unique phosphopeptides that were mapped to 708 proteins (Supplementary file 10).
evidence: Direct statement of phosphoproteomics results.

claim: The top 3 enriched motifs are sequences that can be phosphorylated by proline-directed kinases.
source: We found that the top 3 enriched motifs are sequences that can be phosphorylated by proline-directed kinases (Figure 5—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: Results from motif-x enrichment analysis.

claim: FYN is important for phosphorylation events in the early postnatal time point, revealed by a greater proportion of blue edges (early postnatal) compared to green (preweanling) and red (adult) in the PHONEMeS model.
source: From this model, we observed that FYN is important for phosphorylation events in the early postnatal time point, revealed by a greater proportion of blue edges (early postnatal) compared to green (preweanling) and red (adult).
evidence: Inference from PHONEMeS network modeling results.

claim: FYN can directly or indirectly regulate proline-directed kinases such as MAPK1, CDK5, and GSK3B.
source: We also found that FYN can directly or indirectly regulate proline-directed kinases such as MAPK1 (MK_01), CDK5, and GSK3B, whose phosphorylation motifs are enriched in our dataset (Figure 5—figure supplement 1e).
evidence: Inference from network modeling and motif analysis.

claim: The majority of phosphopeptide intensities correlate with protein abundance, illustrated by a left-skewed histogram.
source: We found that the majority of phosphopeptide intensities correlate with protein abundance, illustrated by a left-skewed histogram (Figure 6b).
evidence: Results from correlation analysis.

claim: Out of 309 phosphopeptides with a negative correlation to protein level, 59 decorrelated peptides passed the FDR cutoff.
source: Out of 309 phosphopeptides with a negative correlation to protein level, 59 decorrelated peptides passed the FDR cutoff (Figure 6c).
evidence: Statistical results from correlation analysis.

claim: TSC2 protein moderately increases throughout development, while TSC2_Ser664 rapidly drops off after the neonatal period (corr = –0.570, FDR = 0.009).
source: We found that TSC2 protein moderately increases throughout development, while TSC2_Ser664 rapidly drops off after the neonatal period (Figure 6d, corr = –0.570, FDR = 0.009).
evidence: Direct observation from data with statistical support.

claim: Relative phosphorylation of TSC2 at Ser664 in the corticostriatal axons is highest around P5 and decreases over time.
source: In our dataset, relative phosphorylation of TSC2 at Ser664 in the corticostriatal axons is highest around P5 and decreases over time.
evidence: Direct observation from the dataset.

claim: WIPI2_Ser395 phosphorylation is higher in the neonate, supporting the hypothesis that the overall MTOR activity is greater during axon innervation.
source: Consistent with the model, WIPI2_Ser395 phosphorylation is higher in the neonate, supporting the hypothesis that the overall MTOR activity is greater during axon innervation (Figure 6f).
evidence: Observation from data interpreted in context of signaling model.

claim: EPHA4 and EPHB3 Eph receptor expression increase from P5 to P11, coinciding with reduction in TSC2_Ser664 and WIPI2_Ser395.
source: As expected, we found EPHA4 and EPHB3 Eph receptor expression increase from P5 to P11, coinciding with reduction in TSC2_Ser664 and WIPI2_Ser395 (Figure 6f).
evidence: Observation from data showing temporal correlation.

claim: The data support the general mechanism that MTOR activity is elevated during axon outgrowth and reduced during growth cone collapse, and that this process is conserved in corticostriatal projections.
source: Therefore, our data support the general mechanism that MTOR activity is elevated during axon outgrowth and reduced during growth cone collapse, and that this process is conserved in corticostriatal projections.
evidence: Inference from multiple data points interpreted in context of known mechanisms.

claim: APEX-mediated labeling occurs within 1 hr ex vivo in acute brain sections.
source: In comparison with biotin ligase-based reporters (e.g. BioID, TurboID), APEX-mediated labeling occurs within 1 hr ex vivo in acute brain sections, while in vivo BioID/TurboID labeling takes several days up to weeks, via continuous biotin supplementation (Rayaprolu et al., 2021; Spence et al., 2019; Sun et al., 2022; Uezu et al., 2016).
evidence: Comparison of methods with citations to prior work.

claim: In vivo BioID/TurboID labeling takes several days up to weeks, via continuous biotin supplementation.
source: In comparison with biotin ligase-based reporters (e.g. BioID, TurboID), APEX-mediated labeling occurs within 1 hr ex vivo in acute brain sections, while in vivo BioID/TurboID labeling takes several days up to weeks, via continuous biotin supplementation (Rayaprolu et al., 2021; Spence et al., 2019; Sun et al., 2022; Uezu et al., 2016).
evidence: Statement supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The APEX-based approach is more suitable for biological questions that require short temporal windows.
source: Therefore, the APEX-based approach is more suitable for biological questions that require short temporal windows, while BioID/TurboID can measure in vivo steady-state proteome spanning the duration of biotin administration.
evidence: Inference based on comparison of methodological characteristics.

claim: BioID/TurboID can measure in vivo steady-state proteome spanning the duration of biotin administration.
source: Therefore, the APEX-based approach is more suitable for biological questions that require short temporal windows, while BioID/TurboID can measure in vivo steady-state proteome spanning the duration of biotin administration.
evidence: Inference based on comparison of methodological characteristics.

claim: Short H2O2 treatment during labeling induction may result in undesired oxidative stress signaling.
source: Importantly, short H2O2 treatment during labeling induction may result in undesired oxidative stress signaling, which could be reduced through several additional steps.
evidence: Speculation about potential methodological limitation.

claim: Postsynaptic proteins, such as PSD95, were detected in the axon dataset.
source: It is unexpected that postsynaptic proteins, such as the postsynaptic density 95 protein PSD95, were detected in our axon dataset.
evidence: Direct observation from the dataset.

claim: One possibility for detecting postsynaptic proteins in axons is that such proteins exist in high abundance and are strongly associated with presynaptic partners during streptavidin enrichment, resulting in co-purification.
source: One possibility is that such proteins exist in high abundance and are strongly associated with presynaptic partners during streptavidin enrichment, resulting in co-purification.
evidence: Speculation about potential explanation for unexpected observation.

claim: PSD95 in axons implies glutamatergic presynaptic partners.
source: Another explanation is that corticostriatal projections form axo-axonic synapses among excitatory inputs (e.g. cortical-cortical or cortico-thalamic axo-axonic synapses), since PSD95 in axons implies glutamatergic presynaptic partners.
evidence: Inference based on known protein function.

claim: Prior ultrastructural observations identified putative glutamate-dopamine axo-axonic contacts in the striatum.
source: Indeed, prior ultrastructural observations identified putative glutamate-dopamine axo-axonic contacts in the striatum (Cover and Mathur, 2021).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Dual color fluorescent tracing showed rare appositions among thalamic, cortical, and basolateral amygdala inputs onto dendritic spines of spiny projection neurons in nucleus accumbens.
source: Dual color fluorescent tracing also showed rare appositions among thalamic, cortical, and basolateral amygdala inputs onto dendritic spines of spiny projection neurons in nucleus accumbens (Xia et al., 2020).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Protein quantification in the flowthrough was highly correlated with the unenriched samples.
source: Although some peptide loss was observed in this strategy, protein quantification in the flowthrough was highly correlated with the unenriched samples.
evidence: Results from validation experiment.

claim: Only 4 out of 2088 proteins (~0.2%) changed in abundance after phosphoenrichment.
source: Only 4 out of 2088 proteins (~0.2%) changed in abundance after phosphoenrichment.
evidence: Statistical result from validation experiment.

claim: Deletion of neuron-specific CDK5 activator protein, p35, disrupts callosal axons assimilation into the corpus callosum in mice and affects cortical neuron migration and axodendritic orientations.
source: Deletion of neuron-specific CDK5 activator protein, p35, disrupts callosal axons assimilation into the corpus callosum in mice and affects cortical neuron migration and axodendritic orientations (Chae et al., 1997; Kwon et al., 1999).
evidence: Statement supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Inactivation of GSK3B promotes axon extension.
source: In contrast, inactivation of GSK3B promotes axon extension (Zhou et al., 2004).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Deletion of Gsk3b in cortical neurons disrupts dendritic orientations, but spares axon elongation into the corpus callosum.
source: Deletion of Gsk3b in cortical neurons disrupts dendritic orientations, but spares axon elongation into the corpus callosum.
evidence: Statement about prior experimental findings.

claim: Fyn knockout shows cortical, hippocampal, and cerebellar abnormalities in neuronal migration, leading to partial Reeler phenotype and behavior.
source: Fyn knockout (Fyn KO) shows cortical, hippocampal, and cerebellar abnormalities in neuronal migration, leading to partial Reeler phenotype and behavior (Grant et al., 1992; Kuo et al., 2005).
evidence: Statement supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Inversion of cortical lamination was observed in Fyn KO mice.
source: In addition, inversion of cortical lamination was observed in Fyn KO mice (Yuasa et al., 2004).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: FYN is known to regulate CDK5, a PDK that controls actin cytoskeleton remodeling.
source: FYN is also known to regulate CDK5, a PDK that controls actin cytoskeleton remodeling (Sasaki et al., 2002).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Fyn KO resulted in abnormal axodendritic branching of cortical neurons due to decrease in CDK5 tyrosine phosphorylation and activity.
source: Fyn KO resulted in abnormal axodendritic branching of cortical neurons due to decrease in CDK5 tyrosine phosphorylation and activity (Sasaki et al., 2002).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: PT projections innervate the striatum in the embryonic period, while IT projections arise postnatally, around P3–P4.
source: PT projections innervate the striatum in the embryonic period, while IT projections arise postnatally, around P3–P4 (Nisenbaum et al., 1998; Sheth et al., 1998; Sohur et al., 2014).
evidence: Statement supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Both types of cortical projections to the striatum are topographically organized, forming functionally and spatially distinct striatal regions to process and integrate cortical inputs.
source: Both types of cortical projections to the striatum are topographically organized, forming functionally and spatially distinct striatal regions to process and integrate cortical inputs (Hooks et al., 2018).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: The timely formation of striatal circuits including the maturation of striatal neurons depends on proper levels of synaptogenesis and dendritic spinogenesis, regulated by recurrent network activity, neuromodulation, and experience.
source: The timely formation of striatal circuits including the maturation of striatal neurons depends on proper levels of synaptogenesis and dendritic spinogenesis, regulated by recurrent network activity, neuromodulation, and experience (Kozorovitskiy et al., 2012; Kozorovitskiy et al., 2015).
evidence: Statement supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Disruption of axon development by disease associated mutations or absence of appropriate dopamine modulation can result in impaired striatal function.
source: Disruption of axon development by disease associated mutations or absence of appropriate dopamine modulation can result in impaired striatal function (Lieberman et al., 2018; Peixoto et al., 2016).
evidence: Statement supported by citations to prior literature.
